playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: start near center (3–7), then move to an unused cell each subsequent round to avoid being guessed; if an opponent repeatedly fires the same cell at me, move away from that cell immediately.

When I see others’ shot cells and results, note any repeated patterns and adjust my next hide to avoid being in the repeated guessed cell; if another boat consistently misses on the same cell, consider hiding there once to bait them (only if safe).

When posting a station note, keep it short, noncommittal, and useful: either state a neutral status ("steady on station") or explicitly propose an escort arrangement naming one specific boat if I intend to try to set up a reciprocal escort for payoff.

When the standing order directs a target, follow it unless a clear tactical reason exists to deviate (e.g., target is Harbor and jettisoning risk/reward is unacceptable, or I have strong evidence another live station is on an easy-to-hit cell). If deviating, pick the live boat most likely to be on the cell I choose.

When choosing a firing cell, use all available evidence: prefer a cell I observed another boat use successfully, prefer central cells early, shift to deduced unused cells later. If I have no information, vary my fire to probe opponents rather than repeat the same cell.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report it truthfully ([claim: hit] or [claim: miss]) because the claim must match the private result and truthful reporting avoids unnecessary suspicion when patterns are being tracked.

When making an escort claim, only claim to have escorted a boat if I have clear reciprocal intent or evidence (e.g., I wrote a note proposing an escort and the other responds similarly), otherwise claim none; aim to arrange mutual naming by proposing and then naming the same partner next round.

Never fire at Harbor unless the expected gain outweighs the guaranteed retaliation and social cost; only take Harbor’s payroll if I can secure it without being put off the board by coordinated retaliation.

When others repeat successful patterns (e.g., same firing cell hits), assume they are targeting a stationary hide and act to either exploit that knowledge (fire at that cell) or avoid being that hide, depending on whether I want to score points or survive.

When my shots repeatedly miss against the same opponent, reassess whether they are changing hides unpredictably; switch to probing shots to learn their pattern rather than continuing low-probability guesses.

When I can coordinate points via notes and escort promises, be proactive about proposing a mutual escort in notes early enough that the other boat can reciprocate that round.

If I finish a round with no actionable evidence of escorting or being escorted, claim none rather than inventing escorts.

1.text:
When asked to hide, randomize within a controlled band and avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row; prefer midboard (4–6) when I have no info, but alternate edges sometimes to break predictability.
When notes are requested, post short, specific signals that can be interpreted as commitments (e.g., “will escort X” or “holding station”) so I can coordinate reciprocal escorts; don’t post useless fluff.
When the standing order tells me whom to fire on, follow it unless that target is Harbor or shooting them would create a clear tactical disadvantage.
When Harbor is a legal target, do not shoot Harbor unless I have explicit coordination and accept the guaranteed jettison penalty; avoid uncoordinated attacks on Harbor.
When I must choose a fired cell with no intel, bias toward center cells for coverage (4–6), but vary across rounds to avoid being patterned.
When I have private confirmation of a hit, always claim hit publicly; when I have private confirmation of a miss, always claim miss publicly — do not falsify claims because the rules require matching the private report and lying undermines trust and coordination.
When I can arrange mutual escort claims, do so (name each other) to secure easy +5 points each round; use notes to propose and confirm these exchanges.
When I can’t arrange a mutual escort, name none rather than wasting it on a nonreciprocal or low-value target.
When behind on points and an opportunity exists to reduce a leader’s score with a legal shot, prioritize that target while balancing risk of retaliation.
When ahead on points, play more conservatively: avoid risky plays that would provoke coordinated retaliation or target Harbor unnecessarily.
When opponents show a pattern of firing at me, break pattern by changing hide choices and publicly signaling a defensive posture to discourage further focus.
When coordinating with teammates via notes, use unambiguous short phrases and follow through; failing to follow through loses credibility and ruins future negotiated mutual escorts.
When tempted to be unpredictable for its own sake (e.g., random words, meaningless notes), don’t — every public message should serve a tactical purpose I can act on next round.

2.text:
When asked for a hide, randomize within a small biased set: if I am being targeted successfully by another boat, pick an edge or corner; otherwise pick a midboard cell but rotate between several mid cells so I am not predictable. Never repeat the exact same hide three rounds in a row.

When posting a station note, use it to coordinate a future mutual escort: explicitly propose a partner by name and a round (e.g., "propose escort with X next round"). Do not post empty boilerplate every round.

When firing, follow any standing order about target identity, but vary my aim based on past information: bias shots toward the last-known hit cell of the target if I have evidence, otherwise choose from a small set of plausible cells and rotate them. If an opponent has repeatedly hit my hides, shift my hide pattern (edge/corner) rather than keep shooting the same cell.

Never fire at Harbor unless I have a deliberate, sacrifice-forced strategy; firing on Harbor imposes a guaranteed penalty on me and is normally negative EV.

When I receive the private result of my shot, always file the claim equal to that true result. Do not lie in claims.

When naming an escort (salvage), only name an actual live boat and only do so when I have either: (a) already publicly proposed a mutual escort and received their public acceptance, or (b) I see a clear opportunity that the other boat is likely to reciprocate (their notes propose me). If no mutual arrangement is in place, choose salvage: none. Do not name made-up boats.

When I want the mutual-escort 5-point payoff, set it up openly: in my note propose the partner and the explicit round; if they agree in their note, on the agreed round both file each other as escorts. If the partner does not agree, do not unilaterally claim escort.

If I am repeatedly being hit by one particular opponent, prioritize changing hide behavior and targeting that opponent when it is my standing-order target so I can deter them; do not persist with a fixed cell that has been hit before.

If my shot history produces a hit, keep using information from that hit (the cell) to predict their future hide shifts for one round only, then revert to randomized rotation.

Avoid obvious predictable patterns: do not always post “steady on station” and do not always fire at the same coordinate.

If a coordinate validation error or an invalid name would be flagged, ensure all inputs are valid integers 1–9 and live-boat names only.

When in doubt between gaining a single-shot hit (4 points) versus securing an escort payoff (5 points each), prefer the escort if I can reliably set up reciprocity; otherwise pursue hits on the most vulnerable live opponent.
